candidate.product: Phoenix Trello — a Trello tribute built with Elixir, the Phoenix Framework, React and Redux

evidence.contradiction: The repository root LICENSE file at the pinned revision carries verbatim MIT text and GitHub's detection agrees, but package.json at the same revision declares "license": "ISC". These two declarations disagree.
evidence.unknownPreserved: This unit does not resolve which declaration governs. Had the candidate reached acquisition, that contradiction would itself have needed a rights decision before admission; it is recorded rather than silently resolved in MIT's favour.

evidence.reduxShape: actions/ (7 modules), reducers/ (8 modules), store/, constants/, containers/, routes/
evidence.backendShape: Phoenix application with 5 Ecto models (user, board, list, card, card_member, comment), 6 API controllers under web/controllers/api/v1, and 2 realtime channels (board_channel, user_channel)
evidence.assessment: By shape this is a working application rather than a scaffold: it has authentication, a REST API, a relational data model, and Phoenix channels for realtime board updates. Its origin, however, is a published tutorial series, and at 39 frontend modules and roughly 70 KB of source it sits at the small end of what the portfolio calls a substantive production application. Recorded as marginal rather than pass, and not relied on, because a hard gate fails below.

evidence.detail: The pinned revision targets React 0.14, a full major generation below the gate's floor. React 0.14 predates the react/react-dom split conventions the portfolio's migration spine assumes, and no revision in this repository reaches React 15: the only other branches are an Elm rewrite and a Hound test-tooling branch, and every tag is older than the pinned head.

evidence.bundlerShape: single entry (web/static/js/application.js plus web/static/css/application.sass) emitting into priv/static, babel-loader with the react/es2015/stage-2/stage-0 presets, extract-text-webpack-plugin@1 for CSS, DedupePlugin and UglifyJsPlugin under NODE_ENV=production
evidence.detail: webpack 1 satisfies the 'webpack at most 4' gate. Recorded for completeness; it does not offset the React version failure.

journeys: Register an account and sign in (views/registrations, views/sessions, actions/registrations.js, actions/sessions.js, api/v1/registration_controller.ex, api/v1/session_controller.ex)
Create and open a board, then add lists and cards to it (views/boards, components/boards, components/lists, actions/boards.js, actions/lists.js, api/v1/board_controller.ex)
Open a card to edit it, comment on it and assign members (views/cards, components/cards, actions/current_card.js, api/v1/card_controller.ex, comment.ex, card_member.ex)
Drag a card between lists with live updates pushed to other viewers of the board (react-dnd@2 with the HTML5 backend, board_channel.ex)
evidence.detail: Recorded for completeness; it does not offset the React version failure.

lockState.detail: The pinned tree contains no JavaScript lock file of any kind. Every dependency is declared with a caret range, so the closure is not reproducible from the repository alone. Recorded as found; no lock was generated and nothing was upgraded.

installBlockers: package.json declares "phoenix": "file:deps/phoenix" and "phoenix_html": "file:deps/phoenix_html". Those paths only exist after the Elixir toolchain has run `mix deps.get`, so `npm install` cannot resolve the manifest in a JavaScript-only cell.
engines pins node 5.3.0 and npm 3.5.x, and devDependencies include node-sass@^3.4.2, whose native binaries were never published for any currently installable Node runtime.
additionalObservations.note: These were observed while reading the manifest for the React gate. No install or build was attempted, because the candidate had already failed a hard gate and attempting a build would have spent budget on a candidate that cannot be admitted.

disposition: Terminal. The React version gate cannot be satisfied by choosing a different revision of this repository, because no revision of it ever reached React 15.
nonclaims: This record establishes no source integrity, dependency closure, build outcome, browser behaviour, migration feasibility, pilot status, production readiness, certification, or legal approval.
No archive was fetched and no blob-level reconciliation against the git tree was performed, so nothing here is source-binding evidence.
The user journeys listed above were inferred from module and controller names in the recursive tree; no browser was run and no journey was observed executing.
The licence reading is a record of the text present at the pinned revision, not a legal opinion, and the MIT-versus-ISC contradiction is left unresolved.
